source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 9.

sections.heading: 1. Life Processes
points: **Life processes** are the basic functions that keep an organism alive: **nutrition, respiration, transport, excretion**.
In animals these are carried out by **organ systems** working together.

sections.heading: 2. Nutrition and Digestion
points: Animals are **heterotrophs** — they take in food made by others.
Steps: **ingestion → digestion → absorption → assimilation → egestion**.
Human path: **mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus**; small intestine absorbs nutrients (**villi**); liver = largest gland.

sections.heading: 3. Respiration
points: **Respiration** breaks down food to **release energy** (in every cell).
**Aerobic** (with oxygen) → CO₂ + water + more energy; **anaerobic** (no oxygen) → less energy + lactic acid/alcohol.
Humans breathe with **lungs**; fish use **gills**; insects use **spiracles/tracheae**.

sections.heading: 4. Circulation and Excretion
points: **Circulation:** the **heart** pumps **blood** (carrying oxygen via **haemoglobin**, food and wastes) through **arteries, veins, capillaries**.
**Excretion:** removal of wastes; **kidneys** filter blood → **urine** (kidneys → ureters → bladder → urethra); **urea** is a key waste.
**Sweat** also removes water and salts.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Life processes: nutrition, respiration, transport, excretion.
Digestion path: mouth → stomach → small intestine (absorption via villi) → large intestine → anus.
Respiration: aerobic (O₂, more energy) vs anaerobic (no O₂, less energy).
Circulation: heart + blood (haemoglobin carries O₂) + arteries/veins/capillaries.
Excretion: kidneys → ureters → bladder → urethra; main waste = urea.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Small intestine** = main site of digestion & absorption (villi); large intestine absorbs **water**.
**Arteries** carry blood **away** from the heart; **veins** carry it **towards** the heart.
**Haemoglobin** (in RBCs) carries **oxygen**.
The **kidneys** filter blood to make **urine** (removing urea).
